assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and reset are modeled as discrete transition events rather than persistent input variables.
hbrg is encoded as int values: 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop.

The phrase 'immediately checks the next destination' is represented by request-triggered outgoing transitions from each floor state after arrival, without adding extra decision pseudo-states because none were explicitly listed.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies initial dispatch to F1, no-request idle at F1, then PS2 starts upward travel to MU2 and S2 arrival stops at F2
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_idle_then_f2_request

scenario_results.description: default-init reaches F1 first, then PS3 starts upward travel to MU3 and reset forces return to stopped F1 from motion
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_to_mu3_then_reset

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F2 checks immediate next-destination workflow: PS3 to MU3, S3 to F3, PS1 to MD1, S1 to F1
scenario_results.name: f2_to_f3_then_down_to_f1_chain

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F2 verifies PS1 selects downward MD1 drive and reset also forces stopped F1 from downward motion
scenario_results.name: f2_request_floor1_then_reset_from_md1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F3 verifies PS2 selects downward MD2 drive and S2 arrival stops at F2
scenario_results.name: f3_request_floor2_via_md2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F3 verifies the global reset forces stopped F1 even from a stopped floor context
scenario_results.name: reset_from_stopped_floor3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at MD2 checks no phantom transition without an arrival sensor, then reset forces stopped F1 from MD2
scenario_results.name: md2_ignores_no_arrival_then_reset

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at MU2 checks no phantom transition without an arrival sensor, then reset forces stopped F1 from MU2
scenario_results.name: mu2_ignores_no_arrival_then_reset

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL requires F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL includes these exact transitions.
NL requires MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2; DSL includes these exact arrival transitions.
NL says hbrg distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop; DSL sets hbrg=1 in MU states, -1 in MD states, and 0 in floor states.
findings.summary: The DSL is highly faithful to the NL elevator FSM: all named floor states, motion states, request-triggered dispatch transitions, arrival-sensor transitions, reset behavior, and hbrg stop/up/down outputs are represented.

evidence: GroundingMap marks all seven leaf states, all ten workflow transitions, reset, initial transition, hbrg, and hbrg enter actions as required and present.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 11 normal transitions including initial, 7 forced reset transitions, 1 variable, and 7 actions.
sim_summary reports 8/8 scenarios passed, including dispatch, arrival, stop output, motion output, and reset cases.
findings.summary: Required components are covered at the state, transition, event, reset, and output-action levels.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary assumption: 'PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and reset are modeled as discrete transition events rather than persistent input variables.'
NL says reset forces F1 'regardless of the outstanding request context', but the DSL has no request-memory variable or queue.
No scenario tests persistent request memory or queued outstanding destinations; all request behavior is event-triggered.
findings.summary: The model does not explicitly store persistent outstanding floor-request context; requests are modeled as discrete events. This is acceptable for the provided NL but leaves a small interpretation gap around the phrase 'outstanding request context'.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary assumption: the immediate check is represented by request-triggered outgoing transitions from each floor state without extra decision pseudo-states.
The DSL permits a new PS event from F1/F2/F3 after arrival and stop.
sim_summary includes a chained scenario F2->MU3->F3->MD1->F1 demonstrating post-arrival next-request behavior.
findings.summary: The simplification of 'immediately checks the next destination' into direct outgoing request transitions from floor states is reasonable and documented, not a blocking oversimplification.

evidence: NL requires reset to force the controller back to floor 1 regardless of outstanding request context.
DSL uses '! * -> F1 :: reset;' and floor-state entry action sets hbrg=0.
sim_summary includes reset from MU3, MD1, MD2, MU2, and F3, all returning to F1 with hbrg=0.
findings.summary: Reset behavior matches the NL requirement and is not an unsafe recovery defect under this review boundary.

evidence: DSL has no label-only decorative '! *' states; '! * -> F1 :: reset' is a global forced transition, not a state-mode label.
design_diagnostics_summary has only W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg and classifies it as advisory.
hbrg is used in entry actions as an output signal, so lack of guard use is not by itself a model defect.
findings.summary: No meaningful structural smell is present. The global forced reset expands into forced transitions in inspection, but it is aligned with the NL. hbrg being unreferenced in guards is expected because it is an output.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary advisory item: W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg.
NL describes hbrg as an output distinguishing drive/stop conditions, not as an internal guard variable.
warning_budget_exhausted is empty and budget_remaining is 2.
findings.summary: No unjustified warning fix is indicated. The unreferenced-variable warning should not drive a repair because hbrg is intentionally a pure output.

evidence: GroundingMap required elements are broadly present in the DSL.
design_diagnostics_summary ok=true with blocking_count=0.
sim_summary ok=true with 8/8 scenarios passed.
five_component_summary is empty, limiting independent component-level evidence.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate. No quality cap is warranted because required states, transitions, reset, and output actions are present and simulations pass. Not T4 because persistent request-context semantics are not explicitly modeled and five_component_summary is empty.
